questionText:
Consider the following languages:

I. $\{a^m b^n c^p d^q \mid m + p = n + q, \text{ where } m, n, p, q \ge 0\}$
II. $\{a^m b^n c^p d^q \mid m = n \text{ and } p = q, \text{ where } m, n, p, q \ge 0\}$
III. $\{a^m b^n c^p d^q \mid m = n = p \text{ and } p \neq q, \text{ where } m, n, p, q \ge 0\}$
IV. $\{a^m b^n c^p d^q \mid mn = p + q, \text{ where } m, n, p, q \ge 0\}$

Which of the languages above are context-free?
explanation:
Language I: $\{a^m b^n c^p d^q \mid m + p = n + q, \text{ where } m, n, p, q \ge 0\}$
Rewriting the condition gives $m - n = q - p$. A Pushdown Automaton (PDA) can push $a$'s onto the stack and pop them for $b$'s to keep track of $m - n$. Then, it can push $c$'s and pop $d$'s to verify $q - p = m - n$. Since a PDA can recognize this language, Language I is context-free.

Language II: $\{a^m b^n c^p d^q \mid m = n \text{ and } p = q, \text{ where } m, n, p, q \ge 0\}$
This language is the concatenation of two context-free languages: $L_1 = \{a^m b^m \mid m \ge 0\}$ and $L_2 = \{c^p d^p \mid p \ge 0\}$. Since Context-Free Languages are closed under concatenation, Language II is context-free.

Language III: $\{a^m b^n c^p d^q \mid m = n = p \text{ and } p \neq q, \text{ where } m, n, p, q \ge 0\}$
This requires comparing three variables simultaneously ($m = n = p$). A single pushdown automaton cannot perform multiple independent stack comparisons. Thus, Language III is not context-free.

Language IV: $\{a^m b^n c^p d^q \mid mn = p + q, \text{ where } m, n, p, q \ge 0\}$
The non-linear product constraint $m \times n = p + q$ cannot be recognized by a PDA stack. Thus, Language IV is not context-free.

Therefore, I and II only are context-free languages.
